en: Theragāthā 3.8 Tikanipāta, Paṭhamavagga The Elder Cūḷa-Panthaka I am not one who has attained the goal, nor am I one who has reached the summit; I am not one who has crossed over, nor am I one who has gone beyond. But I am one who has entered the stream, one who has transcended all suffering. Thus do I declare myself to be a stream-enterer, no longer subject to rebirth in the lower realms. The Verse of the Elder Vassika “Even a single person who is faithful and wise,
among kinsmen here who lack faith— ”
Established in the Dhamma and perfected in virtue,
he brings about the welfare of his kinsmen;
having restrained them out of compassion, he acts for their benefit.
My kinsmen were urged by me;
out of love for their relatives and kin,
they performed services for the monks.
They have passed away and died;
they have attained the happiness of the triple heaven—
